clean.pr_title: perf(router): share null object creation
clean.pr_body:
### Summary

This introduces an internal, non-exported `createNullObject()` helper in `src/internal/utils.ts` and uses it for the null-prototype objects created by `RegExpRouter` and `TrieRouter`.

Repeated `Object.create(null)` calls are large enough that sharing them behind a small internal helper produces a clear and measurable reduction in the minified bundle. The helper is internal implementation detail and is not added to Hono's public API.

### Bundle size

Measured with esbuild using `--bundle --minify --format=esm --target=es2022`, compared with the parent branch:

| Entry point | Before | After | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `src/index.ts` | 18,179 bytes | 17,973 bytes | **-206 bytes** |
| `src/router/reg-exp-router/index.ts` | 6,025 bytes | 5,861 bytes | **-164 bytes** |
| `src/router/trie-router/index.ts` | 2,793 bytes | 2,775 bytes | **-18 bytes** |

The minified-size benefit is concrete, but the runtime trade-off is less universal.

### Runtime considerations

Calling `createNullObject()` introduces a JavaScript function boundary around `Object.create(null)`. A JIT may inline it, but whether and when that happens can depend on the runtime, warm-up state, and call site. Hono supports multiple runtimes, so the result should not be assumed to be identical everywhere.

This PR applies the helper consistently within `RegExpRouter` and `TrieRouter`, including an allocation performed during TrieRouter matching. It does not attempt to replace every `Object.create(null)` in the project, nor does it establish that doing so would always be runtime-neutral.

Future replacements should be evaluated individually, considering:

- the measured minified-size reduction
- whether the call is on an initialization, registration, build, or request-time path
- possible differences between runtimes
- benchmarks when a performance-sensitive path is affected

## Important: this must not become a style rule

My biggest concern is that this helper could become a de facto style rule, leading to context-free automated or AI-generated PRs that mechanically replace every `Object.create(null)`. I strongly want to avoid that outcome; each use should remain a deliberate decision backed by size measurements and runtime considerations.

- [x] `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` to format the code

clean.pr_body:
### Description

Extends agent detection so the User-Agent header can identify more third-party coding agents driving `gh`. Adds nine new agents and an extra environment-variable signal for one existing one.

### Key Points

New agents detected: antigravity, augment-cli, replit, goose, cowork, cursor, cursor-cli, kiro, and pi. One existing agent gains an extra signal: claude-code also matches `CLAUDE_CODE`.

Detection order encodes confidence. `AI_AGENT` still wins, followed by agent-specific variables. Two signals are deliberately low-confidence and ranked accordingly:

- `REPL_ID` is present throughout any Replit environment, not only when a Replit agent drives the CLI, so it is annotated as broad in the code.
- `GOOSE_PROVIDER` only means Goose is configured as a model provider, not that it is running, so Goose is checked absolutely last and any stronger signal wins.

The single-source block now matches precisely instead of loosely: `kiro` is an exact `TERM_PROGRAM` match, and `pi` is anchored to a path boundary (`/.pi/agent`, or the Windows `\.pi\agent`) so an incidental substring cannot trigger it.

We considered a Devin signal and dropped it. The only reliable marker is the existence of a `/opt/.devin` directory, and this detector is intentionally environment-only with no filesystem access. The environment-variable alternatives (for example an `EDITOR` substring) could produce false positives, and Devin's developer-terminal footprint is small, so a noisy signal was not worth the telemetry pollution.

### Notes for reviewers

Two files change. Start in the [`agents` detector](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/1d4ca33b34646ce1165067377fd89f01148cbaf3/internal/agents/detect.go): the constant block lists the new identifiers, and `detectWith` runs the ordered checks top to bottom, returning on first match. Read it straight down to see the precedence. Then the [detector tests](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/1d4ca33b34646ce1165067377fd89f01148cbaf3/internal/agents/detect_test.go) add table cases for every new agent and signal, plus the precedence and negative cases (exact `kiro`, path-boundary `pi`, Goose losing to stronger signals).

First-party documentation for each signal lives inline next to its check, or is marked `// No first-party docs` where none exists.

It still runs `go mod tidy` and `go fix ./...` and updates the golangci-lint and govulncheck pins, but it no longer runs tests, golangci-lint, or govulncheck. When initial multi account support was added to `gh` in `v2.40.0` (December 2023, so almost 3 years ago at this point), we had to perform some [data migrations](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/7f0590c2b8050bb04c5af52291062e6825dda9df/docs/multiple-accounts.md#data-migration). The code for this, with lots of nice explanations can be found in [multi-account.go](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/7f0590c2b8050bb04c5af52291062e6825dda9df/internal/config/migration/multi_account.go), and it has been running on every invocation of `gh` for 3 years: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/7f0590c2b8050bb04c5af52291062e6825dda9df/internal/ghcmd/cmd.go#L136-L142

The TL;DR was that we needed to take host level user/token data and namespace it by username. For example, a hosts entry of:

```
//	github.localhost:
//	  user: monalisa
//	  git_protocol: https
//    oauth_token: xyz
```

would become:

```
// github.localhost:
//	 user: monalisa
//	 git_protocol: https
//   oauth_token: xyz
//   users:
//	   monalisa:
//	     oauth_token: xyz
```

A similar operation would occur for the keyring with a key of:

```
"gh:" + hostname
```

being copied to:

"gh:" + hostname + ":" + username

This set the stage for `gh auth switch` to pick the user and token from a list and "activate" them in the config/keyring entry. The data format was both backwards **and** forwards compatible, to allow users to move back and forward between versions without breaking anything. However, this global keyring entry has been the source of a number of bugs such as:
 * https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/14370
 * https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/12885

These bugs occur because people use `GH_CONFIG_DIR` to swap config files (and therefore active users). This can cause a split brain in some cases where the active user in the config, and the user owning the token in the keyring aren't the same. We can fix the code paths, but we're now 3 years on and I don't think we should give much concern to compatability pre `v2.40.0`, so I want to remove that keyring entry altogether.

This PR doesn't do that work, but it does remove the migration that circles the area and just sits there as debt.

clean.pr_body:
Layer 2 of a stacked dependency upgrade. Stacked on #7571.

Moves the workspace from pnpm **10.33.1 to 12.4.1**. That spans two majors, and v11's config changes mean this is not a one-line bump.

### `.npmrc` is deleted
Since v11, pnpm reads *only* auth/registry settings from `.npmrc`; everything else must live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Our `.npmrc` had no auth settings at all, so it goes away and its contents move over in camelCase:

| `.npmrc` (before) | `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (after) |
| --- | --- |
| `public-hoist-pattern[]` ×5 | `publicHoistPattern` |
| `side-effects-cache=false` | `sideEffectsCache: false` |
| `strict-peer-dependencies=false` | `strictPeerDependencies: false` |
| `prefer-workspace-packages=true` | `preferWorkspacePackages: true` |
| `link-workspace-packages=true` | `linkWorkspacePackages: true` |
| `node-options=--no-warnings` | `nodeOptions: --no-warnings` |

### `allowBuilds` needs an explicit verdict per package
v11 defaults `strictDepBuilds` to `true`, so the familiar "Ignored build scripts: …" warning is now a hard `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` that fails the install. Every package listed as `false` **was already being skipped under pnpm 10** — this records the existing (green) behaviour rather than changing it. `esbuild` keeps the `true` it already had.

If any of these actually should run their install scripts, this is a good place to say so — but that's a behaviour change and deliberately not part of this PR.

### Also
- `pnpm/action-setup` v5 → v6.
- The lockfile gains a `packageManagerDependencies` section — v12 pins pnpm itself from the `packageManager` field. Package resolution is otherwise untouched; v12 consumes the existing lockfile as-is.
- `packages/client/bin/intent.js` picks up its executable bit, which pnpm now sets for declared bins.

v11 also enables `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` (a package must be 24h old to resolve) and `blockExoticSubdeps` by default. Both are kept — they're worthwhile supply-chain defaults and the current lockfile passes them.

### Railway services move from Nixpacks to Railpack
Nixpacks provisions pnpm through corepack, which doesn't install pnpm 12 — so both `trpc-sse-and-websockets` preview deploys fail on this commit under the old builder. Nixpacks is deprecated anyway; Railpack reads the `packageManager` field directly.

```diff
  "build": {
-   "builder": "NIXPACKS",
+   "builder": "RAILPACK",
```

in both `examples/.railway/next-prisma-websockets-starter/railway.json` and `examples/.railway/next-sse-chat/railway.json`. This is the one part of the PR I can't verify locally — Railway has to run it — so the deploy checks on this PR are the test.

### Verification
Verified against a **clean** install (`node_modules` removed, `CI=true pnpm install`, i.e. the frozen-lockfile path CI takes). `pnpm build`, `typecheck-packages`, `typecheck-www`, `lint` and `manypkg check` all pass; `pnpm test` is 1130/1131 with only the pre-existing `httpSubscriptionLink.memory.test.ts` WeakRef/GC failure that also fails on `main`.

clean.pr_body:
### Description

`vi.resetAllMocks()` iterates `REGISTERED_MOCKS`, which holds a `WeakRef` to every mock ever created in the worker, and calls `mockReset()` on each one that is still alive. Its cost therefore grows with the number of live mocks, not with the number of mocks a test actually touched.

With `isolate: false` this becomes the dominant cost of a run. One worker executes many test files, so module-level mocks and every `vi.fn()` that is still reachable keep accumulating. `deref()` also adds each mock to the WeakRef "keep during job" list, so the mocks a test created cannot be collected until the runner yields to the event loop, which rarely happens inside a file. With `mockReset: true` every test then pays for every mock in the worker.

Measured on a large suite (364 files, 6733 tests, `pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: false`, `mockReset: true`, coverage off, 4 workers):

| Vitest                             | wall time | `resetAllMocks()` CPU across workers | max mocks visited per reset |
| ---------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| 4.1.11 (`Set` of strong refs)      | 671 s     | 1838 s                               | ~110,000                    |
| 5.0.0 (`WeakRef` registry, #11092) | 189 s     | 465 s                                | ~66,000                     |
| 5.0.0 + this change                | 26 s      | 0.4 s                                | 5 to 50                     |

The last row was measured with the first commit (strong `Set`s). With the weak-ref version the same suite takes 22.5 s wall time against 24.9 s for the first commit, measured back to back; see the comments below.

This PR applies the approach #11092 introduced for `clearAllMocks()` to `resetAllMocks()`:

- `DIRTY_MOCK_STATES` already tracks mocks that were called since their last `mockClear()`.
- A new `DIRTY_MOCK_CONFIGS` set tracks mocks whose config changed since their last `mockReset()`: `mockImplementation`, `mockImplementationOnce`, `withImplementation`, and `mockName` add the mock, `mockReset()` removes it. Every `mockReturnValue*`, `mockResolvedValue*`, `mockRejectedValue*`, and `mockThrow*` helper goes through one of these.
- `resetAllMocks()` iterates the two sets. `mockReset()` removes the mock from both, so a mock present in both is visited once.

A mock that is in neither set is already in its reset state, so behavior is unchanged. `clearAllMocks()` is unaffected: it still only touches `DIRTY_MOCK_STATES`, and a mock that was reconfigured but never called stays in `DIRTY_MOCK_CONFIGS` until `resetAllMocks()` sees it (covered by the new tests).

~~With this change nothing reads `REGISTERED_MOCKS` anymore, so the `WeakRef` registry and the `FinalizationRegistry` are removed. That also removes the per-mock `WeakRef` allocation and the `deref()` pass that pinned every live mock for the rest of the job. If you prefer to keep the registry for future use, that part of the diff can be dropped; the perf gain comes from the two loops in `resetAllMocks()`. The Firefox 79 note in `docs/guide/browser/index.md` that #11092 added for `WeakRef` support may no longer be needed after this; I left the docs untouched.~~

**Update (second commit, see the comments below):** the paragraph above no longer applies. Both dirty sets hold `WeakRef`s, and the `FinalizationRegistry` from #11092 stays and removes collected mocks from both sets. A mock gets its `WeakRef` the first time it is called or configured instead of at creation, so mocks that are never touched no longer get one; the `REGISTERED_MOCKS` set that held a ref to every mock is gone. Collectability of unused mocks is unchanged from #11092; this PR is about the iteration cost of `resetAllMocks()`, see #11197 (comment) by @hi-ogawa. The docs note on `WeakRef` support stays. The third commit merges `main` and adopts the `Set.prototype.add` guard from #11299 in the shared `markDirty` helper.

Related: #9492, #11092.

clean.pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Part of https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13173 (just adding CI support).

---

I'm not sure what to do about the `base64` changes in the stdlib, which affects our `Base64UrlBytes` type:
1. [`base64.urlsafe_b64decode()`](https://docs.python.org/3.15/library/base64.html#base64.urlsafe_b64decode) now raises a deprecation warning when `+` and `/` is present in the input (the point being that users of this function are expected to pass an input that is using `-` and `_` instead). 
    However, our docs currently say:

    https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/5f49d856043b668321b44f56ed8c440f750bd76b/pydantic/types.py#L2840-L2844
   I don't really understand the last sentence, it seems that we explicitly documented `urlsafe_b64decode()`'s behavior when `+` and `/` are present in input, and that they would be accepted.

2.  [`base64.urlsafe_b64decode()`](https://docs.python.org/3.15/library/base64.html#base64.urlsafe_b64decode) no longer requires the input to be padded. There's no explanation for this change. [python/cpython#73613 (comment)](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/73613#issuecomment-4171000832) says:

    > The default value is True, except in `base64.urlsafe_b64decode()`. So, padding of input no longer required in `base64.urlsafe_b64decode()` by default.

More generally, we will likely be subject to these kind of changes in the future (e.g. https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/148204), and I'm not sure what should be done in these cases (we can try to preserve backwards compatibility on our side -- with non trivial workarounds e.g. for the change 1. -- or follow what the stdlib does, but with expected breaking changes).

clean.pr_body: ## Why we make these changes Replace repeated precision-recall and ROC threshold scans with one shared private iterator: a score-only sorted sweep of cumulative counts. Inputs without NaN take O(n log n), rather than O(n times unique thresholds). This follows the benchmark foundation [#9926](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/9926) and its [successful merged-main CodSpeed baseline](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/actions/runs/37533106982). No linked issue exists. ## New public surface None. Only `pydantic_evals/pydantic_evals/evaluators/report_common.py` and the existing `tests/evals/test_report_evaluators.py` change; no benchmarks, dependencies, APIs, or native code change. ## User-visible behavior ```diff pydantic_evals/pydantic_evals/evaluators/report_common.py :: PrecisionRecallEvaluator.evaluate() -└─ repeated full scans at each threshold +└─ pydantic_evals/pydantic_evals/evaluators/report_common.py :: _iter_threshold_counts() pydantic_evals/pydantic_evals/evaluators/report_common.py :: ROCAUCEvaluator.evaluate() -└─ repeated full scans at each threshold +└─ pydantic_evals/pydantic_evals/evaluators/report_common.py :: _iter_threshold_counts() ``` Original unique thresholds, including the first signed zero, are preserved. Complete ties and infinities use ordinary comparisons; any NaN falls back to the original scans. Extraction, anchors, chart-point creation, AUC arithmetic, and downsampling stay unchanged. ## Verification - Five focused public-output inline snapshot cases in [`test_curve_threshold_counting`](https://github.com/Kludex/pydantic-ai/blob/67cf88ca90ac150e5de977312891ee931016d3dc/tests/evals/test_report_evaluators.py#L355-L437) and [`test_curve_threshold_counting_with_nan`](https://github.com/Kludex/pydantic-ai/blob/67cf88ca90ac150e5de977312891ee931016d3dc/tests/evals/test_report_evaluators.py#L440-L470) pin ties, both first-signed-zero orders, positive/negative infinity, and NaN comparison counts and denominators. Golden values were recorded against the unchanged baseline `402a2eddbafc5445472f9c4f951431652ffb204d`; the copied evaluator oracle and broad matrix were removed in response to review. - Local validation: 65 targeted existing/new evaluator and benchmark tests passed. Strict affected-test Pyright reported zero errors; Ruff and pre-commit passed. - Pre-push source review of `402a2eddb...67cf88ca90ac150e5de977312891ee931016d3dc` found no findings. - The [CodSpeed report for the previous head `66c69d8`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/9959#issuecomment-6038938124) measured approximately 66x faster large precision-recall and 120x faster large ROC against `main` (`e3afea5`). The production sweep is unchanged in `67cf88c`; its [CI](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/actions/runs/37634696684) and [CodSpeed](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/actions/runs/37634696236) checks are pending, not completed results. ## What changes for existing users Large evaluations are faster; existing user outputs and the public API are unchanged. ### Checklist - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver. Not applicable: outputs and public API are unchanged. - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases). ## AI Disclaimer This PR was developed with the assistance of either Claude or Codex. I've reviewed and verified the changes.

clean.pr_body:
### Description

`coverage`, `attachmentsDir`, and `mergeReportsLabel` were copied from the root config to projects in three different places: `resolveTestConfig` (coverage), the `vitest:project` plugin's `configResolved` hook (coverage again, plus `attachmentsDir`), and a one-off `mergeReportsLabel` assignment in `resolveSingleProjectEntry`. The copies now live in `resolveTestConfig` only: `coverage` keeps its existing early assignment (it is shared by reference so projects append to the shared `coverage.exclude`), and `attachmentsDir`/`mergeReportsLabel` are assigned at the end of the resolution. The `configResolved` copies were redundant: nothing reads the Vite-level `test` values between the project's Vite resolution and `resolveTestConfig`.

The advanced guide gains a "Project Configuration Resolution" section documenting how `startVitest`/`createVitest` arguments interact with projects: what `extends` does and does not carry (the config file only, not `viteOverrides` or CLI options), which option groups reach every project regardless of `extends`, and why `plugins` only transfer through a config file.

clean.pr_body:
Serves Vitest's own pre-built modules with `Cache-Control: immutable` instead of having every tester iframe revalidate them.

Vitest's framework assets only change with the Vitest version and browser contexts don't outlive the run, so revalidating them per iframe is wasted work. They are now pinned as `public,max-age=31536000,immutable`. Skipped when `persistentContext` is enabled, since its disk cache would survive a Vitest upgrade.
